title: How knots build an order: growing a line
claim: A constraint excluding a two-change state while allowing every threshold must straddle both changes; knots within windows of r places cannot make a line for n >= r + 1; growing a line at an end needs a constraint holding the start and the new distinction and one holding the current end and the new distinction (one knot per step: B(start, end, new), the start a hub); inserting between neighbours needs only them, a single betweenness knot keeps a line at exactly m + 1 placements (exhaustive check for other knot kinds), inward growth has no hub; the states name every placement and store no direction; the line is pairwise with an exact ruler 2|i - j|; box-triple betweenness on a grid allows exactly its row and column cuts (d = 2 L1, two independent orders).
standard_statement: Betweenness relations of linear orders (Huntington-Kline, Fishburn); cut/split systems of paths and grids (Buneman, median graphs); Opatrny NP-completeness of general betweenness.
prior_work: Huntington and Kline 1917; Huntington 1924; Fishburn 1971; Buneman 1971; Opatrny 1979; OPEN-END-GROWTH-20261107-001; DISTANCE-ORDER-20261117-001.
completion_gate: check.py passes (straddle lemma on random constraints, local windows, insertion), the referee reviews the proofs.
